 'I may not return alive': Imran Khan asks courts for treatment, says 22-hour isolation is killing him 
 Trending Thailand Fire Donald Trump MetLife Stadium Fire Deborah Bergamini Nikhil Gupta Manx Shearwaters Iran war Thailand Fire Donald Trump MetLife Stadium Fire Deborah Bergamini Nikhil Gupta Manx Shearwaters Iran war Thailand Fire Donald Trump MetLife Stadium Fire Deborah Bergamini Nikhil Gupta Manx Shearwaters Iran war 'I may not return alive': Imran Khan asks courts for treatment, says 22-hour isolation is killing him 
 Edited by Prisha Patnaik / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 21:07 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print File photo: Imran Khan Pakistan 's jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has appealed to the country's top courts for urgent medical treatment for himself and his wife, warning that his health has deteriorated to the point where he fears he may not survive. In an open letter, Khan alleged that authorities had ignored earlier court directions on his treatment and described being held in solitary confinement for up to 22 hours a day. The letter, addressed to the chief justices of the Pakistan’s Federal Constitutional Court, the country’s Supreme Court and Islamabad high court, was shared on X by his lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar. Safdar had met Khan at Adiala jail on November 11, when the former prime minister asked him to convey his concerns to the judges. “I spent my life building hospitals so that those who could not afford treatment would receive it free of cost. Today, I ask only that my wife and I be treated,” Khan wrote. Khan claims prolonged isolation has affected his health 
 In the letter, Khan alleged that he had been kept disconnected from the outside world, with no access to family members, lawyers, telephone calls to his sons, books or television. He said the isolation had lasted for up to 22 hours a day and had taken a serious toll on his mental health. He claimed that his lawyer had been allowed to meet him only four times during the year, while Bushra Bibi, his wife, had met her counsel just once. Khan also alleged that his weekly meeting with his wife had been skipped without explanation and that he had not been allowed to meet his sisters, who he said were in custody. Khan said a jail medical board had recorded his anxiety and recommended more frequent contact with his wife and family, along with access to reading material and television. He alleged that these recommendations had not been followed. “No one in the jail is permitted to respond to me or speak to me, not when I offer them salaam and not when I recite a verse of the Holy Quran,” he wrote, adding that he believed the restrictions were intended to make him ill and break his will. He also said his lawyer had discovered during a meeting on February 10 that he had lost 85% of the vision in his right eye. According to Khan, neither his family nor his legal counsel had been informed about the condition at the time. Blood pressure readings reached 192 and 193, Khan says 
 Khan said his blood pressure had risen steadily during his confinement, from 130 to 150 and then 170, before reaching 192 and 193 on November 10. He said doctors had warned him that he was highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest, and that his heart had already suffered damage. “At seventy-four, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive,” he wrote. Khan said he was writing from a solitary cell because it had become “the only way my voice can leave these walls”. He also rejected the suggestion that he was seeking medical relief as a way to avoid his legal cases, saying he had continued to contest them on their merits. Bushra Bibi could lose her eyesight, he says 
 Khan said his wife's condition was the immediate reason he had decided to write to the courts. According to the letter, Bushra Bibi suffered a retinal detachment in April and underwent what he described as complicated eye surgery in secrecy before being returned to solitary confinement. He said that when he saw her this month, she could neither tolerate light nor open her eyes. Without another operation, he warned, she could lose her sight permanently. Khan alleged that her medical records had been withheld and that she had been denied access to her own doctors. He also raised concerns over her pending request for suspension of sentence. Also check: Two sisters of ex-Pak PM Imran Khan released from jail; elder sister, wife remain behind bars Bushra Bibi has separately approached the courts seeking an examination by an ophthalmologist and permission to receive treatment from doctors of her choice at her own expense. She has said doctors diagnosed her with a mature cataract and advised another eye operation. Khan says Pak SC order on hospital transfer was not followed 
 The former prime minister said the Supreme Court had directed on August 18 that he be shifted to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad within two days. The order also called for a medical board to examine him and for him to be allowed contact with his family, according to the letter. “That order has not been implemented,” Khan wrote. The government had instead taken him to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences for an eye check-up before returning him to prison. Pakistan’s information minister Attaullah Tarar had attributed the change in arrangements to security concerns linked to PTI workers gathering outside the hospital. The PTI denied the allegations and accused the government of disregarding the court's directions. Khan also complained that his medical concerns were not being heard as promptly as other legal matters, saying his appeal in the Toshakhana-2 case was being taken up ahead of older matters concerning his health and the implementation of court orders. He and Bushra Bibi were sentenced to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-2 case, which relates to the purchase of a Bulgari jewellery set gifted to Khan by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit in 2021. Khan said he had faced numerous prosecutions after losing power in a no-confidence vote in 2022, but maintained that he had chosen to fight the cases through the courts. He alleged that the legal system had failed to provide relief when he and his wife needed it most. “I do not ask your Lordships for any favour. All I request as justice is the implementation of the orders of the honourable SC and proper treatment for our medical conditions,” he wrote. He added that he could prove his innocence only if he remained alive, and urged the judges to intervene “before it is too late”. Join conversation

 Khan's sons also reacted to the letter. Kasim Khan described it as devastating to read, while Sulaiman Khan called it “incredibly harrowing” and said his father's demand for medical care was not a request for special treatment. Khan has been in prison since August 2023. Bushra Bibi was arrested in January 2025 in a separate case. Khan denies wrongdoing in the corruption cases against him and says they are politically motivated. Pakistan’s government denies that allegation.
